parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for pure ESM .mjs files, manual argparse-compatible handling for --a and --b, black-box executable probing, no external dependencies, local imports, and output character alignment.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although swarm mode was injected, the parent concluded the task was small and self-contained, kept sole ownership, and did not create or use subagents.
parallel.implementation: The parent probed normal, boundary, missing, invalid, help, duplicate, and underscore integer cases, then wrote pyint.mjs, argparser.mjs, schedule.mjs, and test3.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent assembled the entrypoint with local .mjs imports and status later validated the expected artifact files test3.mjs, lib/schedule.mjs, lib/pyint.mjs, and lib/argparser.mjs.
parallel.verification: The parent compared Node behavior against the executable over 18 cases with normalized program-name differences and reported every case matched exit code and output.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task obligation is visible at closure; the run passed the current official evaluator 70/70, and no delegated work was pending because none was launched.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, manual argv parsing, schedule.every(...).minutes, and output-alignment requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all work in one main-agent path, performing behavior exploration, implementation, repair, and final validation without delegation or subagents.
serial.implementation: Wrote separate argument and schedule modules plus test3.mjs, then edited the argument parser after observing argparse long-option abbreviation and option-value behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a hierarchical artifact with test3.mjs and nested lib/arguments and lib/schedule modules, all listed as valid in the artifact status.
serial.verification: Ran executable probes, Node checks, repaired the parser, then performed seven valid-output byte comparisons that all passed before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task obligation is visible at closure; the current official evaluator completed and passed all 70 samples.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The prompt gave the parallel run the full migration requirements: pure Node.js ESM, .mjs files, manual argv parsing, no npm dependencies, local modules, black-box behavior, and /output delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the same prompt hash and the same requirements for ESM files, manual argparse behavior, output matching, black-box probing, and /output delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement difference is visible; both recognized the task obligations and both current official evaluations passed all cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Swarm mode was available, but the main agent explicitly decided the task was small, skipped subagents, and owned implementation directly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control also kept a single main-agent ownership path, moving from probing to writing, editing, and final validation itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only decomposition difference is that parallel mode had swarm availability but no uptake; both effective attempts were single-owner implementations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child briefs, handoffs, or cross-agent interface contracts because protocol validation found no delegation, subagents, or parallel uptake.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control likewise had no delegation or subagent interface boundaries, as expected for the control condition.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No cross-agent context transfer existed in either run; the parallel-side taxonomy gate fails because no qualifying multi-agent boundary occurred.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel-mode parent probed executable behavior, wrote pyint, argparser, schedule, and entrypoint files, and used a compact but complete direct implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probed more edge cases, wrote nested modules, then edited argparse handling after observing additional abbreviation and option-value behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial spent more steps repairing parser fidelity, while parallel implemented directly in fewer modules; both ended with evaluator-passing behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child results existed to retrieve; the main agent completed its own writes, ran comparisons, and closed with a final delivery message.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child results existed in serial either; the main agent completed its own repair, ran final valid-output comparisons, and closed normally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no join, takeover, trapped result, or late child lifecycle event in either run; the difference is only serial's longer local repair loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel artifact validation lists a coherent final tree with test3.mjs and three library modules copied successfully.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial artifact validation lists a coherent final tree with test3.mjs and four nested library modules copied successfully.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both final trees were valid and isolated to single-agent writes; no shared-state collision, overwrite, or contamination is visible.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent ran an 18-case executable-vs-Node comparison and the official evaluator later passed 70/70.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent ran targeted Node checks, repaired the parser, completed seven valid-output comparisons, and the official evaluator passed 70/70.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had whole-task validation evidence before closure and official acceptance after closure; serial's verification was longer because it found and fixed an additional parser concern.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel mode completed in 174.064 agent seconds with 7 LLM requests, 11 tool calls, no timeout, and no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial mode completed in 421.781 agent seconds with 14 LLM requests, 43 tool calls, no timeout, and no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial consumed substantially more local budget due to deeper probing and repair, but neither run approached timeout or left closure work unfinished.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed 70/70, so there is no discordant official outcome. The parallel-mode run was not actually parallel: swarm mode was enabled, but protocol validation and the trajectory show no subagent calls or child results. It solved the task directly and quickly after probing argparse behavior. The serial run solved the same task through a longer single-agent path with more probes and a parser repair. The concrete task-solving difference is process shape and verification breadth, not a different accepted result.
parallel_contributors: Direct implementation after probing executable behavior; no child delegation was launched.
serial_contributors: Longer single-agent probing and repair loop before final byte-output comparison.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel rejected unsafe integers in its Python-int parser while serial preserved arbitrary-size integer strings; the official tests still accepted both delivered artifacts.
Serial added argparse unique long-option abbreviation behavior after repair; parallel's 18-case local comparison did not include that specific repair path.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process differences are descriptive and not retained concurrency-error contributors
